Conference Queue

Conference Queue (working title)

A virtual queue for parent-teacher conference night. Parents book a 1:1 slot, then track their place in line in real time, replacing the shared sign-up sheet schools use today.

Process

Research

The brief was open, so I spent a day on the market, the user types, and feature ideas.

Competitors

  • QueueBee, queue management for customer waiting lines
  • QRQ, queue management and virtual queue software
  • Queue App, virtual waiting list (Google Play)
  • Clalit, queue and waiting-list setup on an outside service
  • Calendly, meeting scheduling

Possible users

  • Parent-Teacher talk
  • Salon
  • Gov service
  • Medical clinic
  • Buy tickets to something
  • Consultation
  • Hairdresser
  • Restaurant
  • Experience (art exhibit)

Queue types

TypeHow it works
Live queuePeople join as they come, and wait their turn on the spot.
Booked queuePeople reserve a slot before they arrive, then join the queue on the day.

Manager actions

Background

The focused problem

I chose parent-teacher meetings because they usually run on a shared Google Sheet.

A sign-up sheet is a list. What's missing is the queue itself: a live position, and a notification when it's your turn. Parents also need a way to change or edit their slot, and the manager needs a way to get notified.

Target users

Parent, primary

A parent at conference night, often for more than one child, who wants a real estimate of the wait instead of guessing when to walk over.

Teacher or school staff, secondary

The teacher or staff member running the evening, who needs slots filled and the line moving without manual coordination between meetings.

Visitor journey wireframes
1 of 3

From invite link to setting the meeting

The visitor signs in and sets a time slot, and can edit it until the session starts.

Visitor journey wireframes
2 of 3

The session is coming up

As the session is coming up, the session time becomes bigger and clearer. The visitor gets notified of a delay and when they need to come in.

Visitor journey wireframes
3 of 3

Session start to end

During the session, the visitor can see it in progress and gets told when time is almost up. At the end, they can send feedback. Once the session moves to past sessions, the home screen shows an empty state with the option to start their own queue or learn how it works.

Summary

  • The problem: parent-teacher meetings run on a shared Google Sheet, with no live position and no notifications.
  • Users: parents (primary), teachers and school staff (secondary).
  • Scope: parent booking and the live queue, with the teacher side at wireframe level.
  • Journey: book a slot, track the queue, get notified when it's your turn.
  • Next: finish the wireframes and the polished UI screens.
